agree.reason: The page is clear and believable, but an owner paying her cousin $600 a year sees $199 a month and nothing that tells her why it's worth about $2,388 a year, so she probably won't book.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief and the missed deadlines are stated openly, but 'that person already knows your salon' says more than the facts show for a new client.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw facts are listed but never worked: 29 of 31 clients kept (100% of those who didn't sell), 9 of 12 closes on time, and the $800 saving set against the annual cost are all left for the reader to figure out.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative is a relative doing the books once a year at tax time, and the page never describes it: no monthly view, payroll and sales tax handled by someone else or by her, and a year-end catch-up.

qualification.reason: The 10th-of-the-month deadline and the three misses give a date and a number the reader can check, but the page never says what happens to her when the deadline is missed.

objections.reason: It deals with being a one-person business and with the missed deadlines, but not the objection this reader actually has: cost compared with $600 a year, and loyalty to a cousin she's fond of.

fit.reason: About 330 words of main sales-page text with clear sections and a booking button at the end, as the brief asked.
